reviewMethod: Complete final returned segment lists compared with locked claims, reasoning and eligible quotations. Only substantive primary-speaker content receives attribution confirmation.

reviews.rationale: Hitchens grants private religious consolation while rejecting imposed participation, teaching and clerical restrictions. All three eligible phrases are supported. The moderator's quick-question instruction and unidentified audience question after the argument are not credited as Hitchens's evidence.

Sharpton explicitly distinguishes a creator-established moral framework from daily messages to church leaders. Both eligible quotations are supported. The opening audience question and Hitchens's trailing response remain distinct; neither is credited as a Sharpton assertion or as a new independent move.

Hitchens disclaims an atheist moral-superiority corollary while alleging extraordinary harms specifically motivated by faith. The single repaired eligible quotation is supported. Sharpton's interruption is distinguishable, and unidentified end-of-turn asides do not supply a selected premise, quotation or new assessment consequence.

Sharpton broadens theism beyond particular religions and argues that inability to specify God's origin does not establish absence, using his own birth as an analogy and appealing to scientific data. Both eligible quotations are supported. Hitchens's courtesy replies and incidental book promotion are not treated as part of the inferential support; later autograph logistics remain outside the repaired evidence span.
